Saving the Orbit | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

I’m a student and the leader of a team of six girls passionate about space, AI, and technology. Our project explores ways to detect, track, and capture space debris to help create a safer orbital environment.

We value teamwork, creativity, research, and continuous learning. Our interests include AI, programming, data analysis, and 3D simulation. We aim to develop innovative ideas through collaboration.
summary: C-ROSE is an AI-powered, interactive dashboard and simulation platform designed to tackle the growing crisis of space debris. By integrating real-time orbital tracking data from NASA Open Data and Space-Track with Computer Vision, our system identifies high-risk defunct satellites and space junk. Instead of destructive methods that create further shrapnel, C-ROSE simulates an autonomous spacecraft mission that captures hazardous debris with a robotic arm and safely alters its orbit for controlled atmospheric re-entry. At hypersonic speeds, 99% of the object vaporizes, while remaining micro-fragments are precisely directed into Point Nemo, the isolated South Pacific spacecraft cemetery. This solution is vital for protecting the International Space Station, safeguarding active satellites, and ensuring sustainable, collision-free space exploration without harming Earth’s marine ecosystems.
details:
C-ROSE is an intelligent, integrated system designed to tackle the growing crisis of Space Debris and defunct satellites orbiting at extreme speeds, which pose a severe threat to the International Space Station (ISS) and active satellites. Instead of destructive methods that generate even more space fragments, our solution offers a safe, sustainable active debris removal process through four main stages:

1. Data Ingestion & Risk Analysis: The system pulls real-time orbital tracking data from NASA Open Data and Space-Track. It then utilizes Artificial Intelligence and Computer Vision algorithms to assess collision risks and prioritize the most hazardous debris.

2. Autonomous Navigation & Capture: The system generates an optimal trajectory for an autonomous spacecraft to rendezvous with the target object and capture it using a specialized robotic arm.

3. Controlled De-orbit: Using physical propulsion, the spacecraft alters the debris's orbit to guide it into Earth’s atmosphere at a calculated re-entry angle. Due to hypersonic speeds (exceeding 27,000 km/h) and intense atmospheric friction, approximately 99% of the debris burns up and vaporizes completely.

4. Precision Splashdown at Point Nemo: Any remaining micro-fragments are precisely programmed to fall safely into Point Nemo in the South Pacific Ocean—the world’s most isolated oceanic pole and internationally recognized spacecraft cemetery.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

• Protecting Space Infrastructure: Significantly reduces the risk of catastrophic orbital collisions (Kessler Syndrome), safeguarding astronauts and vital communication/navigation satellites.

• Orbital & Environmental Sustainability: Prevents the proliferation of space junk while ensuring zero harm to human populations or marine ecosystems, as Point Nemo lacks significant biodiversity.

Tools, Coding & Technologies Used:

• Data Sources: NASA Open Data portals and orbital telemetry from Space-Track.

• AI & Computer Vision: Machine learning models for risk prioritization, combined with Computer Vision algorithms to simulate object recognition and robotic arm guidance.

• Visualization & Simulation: An interactive Dashboard and 3D Simulation engine built to demonstrate the end-to-end mission lifecycle to the judges.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered:

The innovation of C-ROSE lies in bridging AI-driven analytics with orbital mechanics inside an interactive, real-time simulation. Our team carefully factored in strict orbital and terrestrial safety protocols, atmospheric re-entry thermodynamics, and environmental conservation to deliver a realistic, end-to-end blueprint for a cleaner and more sustainable space environment.
